references.text: Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to a meal, showing the same combination of sacrifice and shared meal that Jethro practiced.
Aaron and the elders of Israel ate and drank in God's presence after the peace offerings were brought, corresponding to how they ate bread with Jethro before God.
The laws concerning peace offerings (זְבָחִים), which included a meal where the offerer and guests ate together before the Lord.
The command to eat before the Lord your God and rejoice, reflecting the holy meal that Jethro held with Aaron and the elders.
Melchizedek, a non-Israelite priest, brought bread and wine and blessed Abram in God's name, showing the parallel to Jethro as a pagan priest who offered sacrifices to God.
Paul refers to those who eat from the sacrifices and have fellowship with the altar, illustrating the same principle of meal fellowship at the sacrifice.
Describes the same historical event where Jethro arrives and then offers sacrifices; the verses illuminate each other as before-and-after scenes in the same account.
Connects the cause (the news of God's salvation in verse 1) with the effect (the offering and meal in verse 12), showing how faith in God's deeds is expressed liturgically.
Represents respectively the invitation to the meeting and the actual performance of the worshipful meal within the same account.
Illuminates the transition from Jethro's historical sacrifice (where Aaron participates) to the fixed, law-established priestly service that Aaron's descendants perform in later times.
Mutual illumination of the concept 'to eat before the Lord's face' as an expression of holy fellowship and God's presence in the context of sacrifice.
Describes respectively the arrival and the subsequent offering within the same sequence of events; they illuminate each other as parts of a unified account.
Illuminates the theme of 'eating holy food before God's face,' but also shows the contrast between the unique fellowship offering with Jethro and the strict priestly service.
